title: Why EVs miss claimed range (Short)
hook: Why your EV never hits its claimed range
youtube_title: Why does your EV never hit its claimed range?
caption:
The brochure says one number, your dashboard says another. Nobody is lying: the claimed figure comes from a lab test, and real Indian roads add highway speed, summer AC and a heavy right foot.

EV owners: what real-world range do you get vs the claim? Tell me your car and number in the comments.

slides.heading: Why your EV never hits its claimed range
Claimed range is a lab test
slides.body: In India, certified figures come from the MIDC test cycle under controlled conditions. Real roads are messier.

slides.heading: Highway speed eats range
slides.body: Air resistance rises sharply with speed. Cruising at 100 km/h uses noticeably more energy than 70 km/h.

slides.heading: Indian summers cost kilometres
slides.body: Cabin AC runs off the same battery. In high heat, the car may also spend energy cooling the battery itself.

slides.heading: Heavy right foot, lower range
slides.body: Hard acceleration burns energy fast. Smooth driving and regenerative braking win some of it back.

slides.heading: Plan with a buffer
slides.body: Many owners plan trips assuming noticeably less than the claim, especially on fast highway runs. Better a spare 50 km than a tense last 5.
